sections.h2: Who handles property tax in Phelps County?
sections.html:
Two offices in the courthouse at 200 N Main Street, Rolla, MO 65401 divide the work. One values the property and the other bills it and takes the money. Neither sets a rate. Voters in each taxing district do that.

  • Assessor: Suite 126, (573) 458-6135, fax (573) 458-6149, weekdays 8:00 to 4:30
  • Collector: Suite 129, (573) 458-6155, collectorgroup@phelpscounty.org, open weekdays through lunch until 4:30
  • County Clerk: (573) 458-6115, for levy and tax rate questions
  • Recorder of Deeds: (573) 458-6095, for the deed itself

The assessor cannot discuss the dollar amount of a bill. That office answers questions about assessed and market value, and the collector handles the rest.

The collector offers two formulas. Divide the assessed value by the adjustment factor to estimate the assessor's market value, then divide the assessed value by 100 and multiply by the levy to get the tax. The assessment rates are 19 percent of market value for residential land, 12 for farmland and 32 for commercial use, as RSMo 137.115 provides.

That assessed figure, counted in hundreds, is multiplied by the combined levy of the school, fire, city and other districts covering your parcel. You pay only the districts that apply to your address, not every levy in the county.

Real estate is valued on a two year cycle, but the 2025 reassessment was larger than usual. The state tax commission found that local values had slipped out of the 90 to 110 percent compliance band after several years of rising sales prices. Average residential assessed value rose by about 10 percent that year, while agricultural and commercial values stayed flat apart from new construction or changes in condition.

sections.h2: If the assessor visits your property
sections.html:
Field staff are canvassing the county to refresh photos of homes and outbuildings and to note condition, concentrating on parcels not visited in more than five years. The work is required by RSMo 137.130. Staff drive white Ford Bronco Sports with the assessor's logo on the doors, wear vests marked Phelps County Assessor and carry a county photo ID. Owners who asked to be called first are called when possible.

State law also limits large jumps. Under RSMo 137.115, a residential parcel cannot rise more than 15 percent without a physical inspection unless new construction explains it, and the owner has at least thirty days after written notice to ask for an interior inspection.

Begin by calling or visiting the assessor at (573) 458-6135 and asking which comparable sales and condition notes support your number. Missouri law favors an owner who disagrees. An increase must be reported to the record owner, who gets a hearing if the county's equalization board reviews it (RSMo 137.180).

Ask the county clerk at (573) 458-6115 for the board's forms and filing deadline. The board begins with no assumption that the assessor is right, and an increase of 15 percent or more outside new construction leaves the burden of proof on the assessor (RSMo 138.060). The next stop is the State Tax Commission, open by the statutory date or thirty days after the board finishes, whichever is later (RSMo 138.430).

Statements go out in early November. December 31 is the last day, and a postmark after it brings late fees. Send mail with the stub, called the statement topper, because it carries the account number. Bank bill pay services often send errors and no topper, so the collector advises against them.

The collector keeps none of the online fees. One check can cover any mix of real estate and personal property statements, but the amount must be exact, because a payment written for the wrong sum cannot be processed. Installment plans exist for real estate and personal property, so ask at the counter for the form. If no bill has arrived by Thanksgiving, call right away.

Phelps County seniors may qualify for a freeze on real estate taxes under Senate Bill 190 as expanded by Senate Bill 756. The applicant must be at least 62 by December 31 of the application year, own and live in the home as a primary residence, and be responsible for its taxes. Only one owner needs to be 62.

Applications are taken from March 1 through May 31. The freeze starts with the 2027 tax year, and the collector asks for at least 90 days to process. After that, participants send an affidavit every year during the same March through May window.

  • The freeze covers one primary residence only and is not retroactive to age 62.
  • It does not carry over to a new home; a move means a new application and a new base year.
  • A transfer of title removes the home from the program, as does a missed annual affidavit.
  • Debt levies and newly voted tax increases still show on the bill.

Questions go to the collector at (573) 458-6155 or seniortaxrelief@phelpscounty.org.

sections.h2: Unpaid taxes and the August auction
sections.html:
Delinquent parcels are auctioned once a year on the fourth Monday in August, starting at 10:00 am in the Community Room of the courthouse, under RSMo 140.150. Notice runs in the Rolla Daily News on three consecutive Wednesdays beforehand, and the list appears on the collector's website.

A buyer does not own the house right away. The owner, a lienholder or an occupant can redeem during the year after the sale by paying the collector the purchase amount and costs, and the buyer earns simple interest of 10 percent a year on the tax and cost portion. The county advertises many more parcels than it sells, because most owners pay before the day arrives. If you are behind, ask the collector what it takes to come off the list before the sale.

For a seller, this matters at the listing stage. Clear any delinquent year before you go under contract, since a title company will want it paid at closing. A cash buyer can still close quickly, though the back tax comes out of your proceeds.

Phelps County is in central Missouri, and Rolla is both the seat and the largest city, home to Missouri University of Science and Technology. Other communities include St. James, Newburg, Doolittle and Edgar Springs. The July 2025 estimate is 45,247 residents and 20,625 housing units, and 61.7 percent of households own their home. A typical home is valued at $206,500, median gross rent is $798 and median household income is $58,396. School districts include Rolla 31, St. James R-I, Newburg R-II and Phelps County R-III.

faqs.q: When must Phelps County real estate tax be paid?
faqs.a: December 31. Bills are mailed in early November, and a payment not postmarked by December 31 incurs late fees.
Not the assessor, who sets value only. Each taxing district sets its levy by a vote of its residents, and the county clerk at (573) 458-6115 can answer rate questions.

faqs.q: Who gets the tax bill if I bought my house mid-year?
faqs.a: The new owner pays the bill when it comes due. The buyer receives a credit at closing for the tax the seller owed for the year, and bills show the previous owner's name if the sale came after September 1.

faqs.q: When can I apply for the senior tax freeze?
faqs.a: Applications are accepted from March 1 through May 31. Call the collector at (573) 458-6155 to confirm the current year's window.

faqs.q: What day is the delinquent tax auction?
faqs.a: The fourth Monday in August at 10:00 am, in the courthouse Community Room in Rolla.
